chunks: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said:

“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم entered upon a man from the Ansar while the wind had afflicted him. He said: ‘O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, how should I perform salat (prayer)?’ So he said:”

“If you are able to seat him, then seat him; otherwise, turn him toward the qiblah, and instruct him to gesture with his head. He should make the sajdah lower than the ruku'. And if he is not able to recite, then recite in his presence and make him hear it.”

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: gesturing by indication in place of full bodily movement
key_terms.الرِّيحُ: a debilitating affliction described as wind that overcame the man
key_terms.يَقْرَأَ: to recite, meaning the recitation required in prayer

ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform salat (prayer) if he cannot stand or recite?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of performing salat (prayer) for a sick person who is physically unable to stand or perform the normal actions. It establishes practical rulings for seated prayer, gesturing with the head, distinguishing sajdah from ruku', and assisting the sick person with recitation when needed.
